svg.title: APL's inhibition of the Kenyon cells as a current and as a conductance, against flies' limits
svg.text: APL as a conductance: graded like flies', and never holding the Kenyon cells past flies' limit
As a current, APL graded like flies' takes the Kenyon cells 21 mV down as an odor begins; as a conductance reversing 20 mV below rest it divides a responding cell's input
more than it pulls a quiet one down: 7.1 mV at most, with flies' graded response (0.45; flies 0.49) and silencing effect (2.92 and 2.21-fold; flies 2-3).
The Kenyon cells' inhibition as 3-octanol begins
time from the odor's onset (s)
mV from where they sit with APL silenced
